newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to up, HSFO gains again.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to up, HSFO gains again.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were steady to up Wednesday in thin trade, with high sulphurs still buoyed by good bunker and export demand despite a sharp selloff in NYMEX crude, industry sources said.

"There has been some export demand, and bunker demand has been average to good, but it's still mostly a barge market, not a cargo market," said one cash trader, adding low sulphur interest could also pick up soon as Florida heats up.
In New York Harbor, high sulphurs inched higher, with 2.2 percent up slightly at $14.50-75 a barrel and three percent scoring a similar gain to $14.25 or better, traders said.
NYH physical one percent was unchanged at $15.00-25 a barrel, with May one percent paper steady at about $15 despite softer crude.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour also was little changed at $16.00-25, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was steady at $15.00-25, while three percent was flat to slightly higher at $13.50.
Traders said high sulphur was helped by reports of a prompt 380 bunker sale at $13.75 (FOB Houston).

New York city gate gas prices gained several cents Wednesday to the mid-to-high $2.30s/mmBtu, or $14.93 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was steady to up slightly at about $2.01/mmBtu, or $12.66 a barrel.
